realtime_memories.content: OpenBroadcast (~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/openbroadcast): Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + hls.js live-TV player over the iptv-org open dataset. Statically prerenders every channel page from a committed data/channels.approved.json snapshot; never calls iptv-org at request time. Pushed to github.com/myselfRaifMondal/openbroadcast (PUBLIC, main) and connected to the Vercel Hobby project (prj_QvYbgDmBaZd4ktme2R5TENoFpE8u, openbroadcast.vercel.app): push to main auto-deploys production, other branches get previews. Verified working — a push produced a Ready production deploy in ~50s. Name 'OpenBroadcast' was inferred from the repo URL the user supplied, not chosen by them — they asked about it 2026-08-30 and did not rename. It appears in app/layout.tsx (metadata title + header wordmark) and README; renaming the Vercel project would change the subdomain and break the current link.

Two catalogue modes, switched by POLICY_MODE. Default 'public' = curated allowlist policy in scripts/policy.ts: four named grounds for inclusion (public + legislative iptv-org categories, reviewed exact-match public-broadcaster owner list, reviewed government-owner regexes), then hard exclusions that always win. 'open' (npm run filter:open) = full catalogue, no licensing or category filtering; INCLUDE_NSFW=1 also keeps adult channels. After pruning dead streams: curated 623 channels / 91 countries (this is what git tracks and the live site serves), open 7,648 / 174 countries.

User wants the full unfiltered catalogue INCLUDING sports and pay-TV — stated 2026-08-30: it is a private media player for personal use, 'don't need to be shy'. They reaffirmed this after I raised the licensing concern, so treat open mode as their standing decision; do not re-litigate it. They had earlier specified the strict public-only filter, so keep both modes working rather than deleting the curated policy.

Open mode must stay honest and must never reach the public URL. Channels with no allow-rule match get basis 'unverified-open-mode' labelled 'No verified licensing basis' rather than inheriting a public-broadcaster justification; header shows an OPEN MODE badge; /policy leads with a banner saying the policy is not applied. CRITICAL now that git auto-deploys: data/channels.approved.json tracked on main is ALWAYS the curated build — committing the open catalogue over it publishes the unfiltered player. The open catalogue lives untracked at data/channels.open.local.json (gitignored); swap it in locally, never commit it. Two hardening options offered but not built: keep open mode on a 'personal' branch (previews are protected by default), or enable Vercel Authentication under Project > Settings > Deployment Protection (free on Hobby; the MCP Vercel connector 404s on this project, so it must be done in the dashboard). Note: two early commits still contain the open snapshot in public history — user was told, declined nothing, no rewrite done.

Maintenance scripts: npm run filter:channels (curated build), filter:open (full catalogue), audit:candidates [minChannels] (owners clearing every hard exclusion but matching no allow rule — the allowlist review queue), check:streams [-- --prune] (two-pass stream probe, writes data/stream-health.json, records a streamHealth summary on the dataset, prunes only genuinely dead and never geo-blocked).

Stream health / dead-channel pruning (measured 2026-08-30, open catalogue). Two-pass probe: 10s timeout at 64-way, then every failure retried at 20s/40-way — the retry recovered 296 of 1,964 apparent failures (15%), so NEVER prune on a single pass. Final: 7,108 live, 540 geo-blocked, 1,668 dead pruned (9,316 -> 7,648 channels, 174 countries, 266 sports). Geo-blocked (403/451) are deliberately NOT pruned — healthy streams the broadcaster fences to its own country; they play in-country or over VPN, and the curated public/government set geo-blocks hardest (15.7% vs 4.4% commercial). Health is a snapshot: iptv-org endpoints rot continuously, so re-run and re-prune periodically. Open follow-up offered but not built: surface health in the UI (sort/grey dead) so the catalogue self-corrects between probes.

Verify player changes against a real stream before claiming they work — Playwright against a running build, reading video.readyState/currentTime/videoWidth, not just an HTTP 200. Why: a channel page returns 200 while the stream is geo-blocked or dead, so status codes prove nothing about playback. Confirmed working probes: ABC News AU, TVR 1, Red Bull TV. Known geo-fenced: Rai 1, TyC Sports.
